issue_context.title: Azure data explorer integration stops
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Azure Data Explorer integration stops sending data to ADX. After restart the logs says xx number of events dropped

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024-06-02

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

azure data explorer

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/azure_data_explorer

### Diagnostics information

This seems to happen when a State on the event-bus is not serializable. ex. the HACS integration Affalddk is not serializable, bur this has also been found in other integrations. The solution is to make the ADX integration more robust to filter these malformed data. As a tested workarround, setting up filters on the entities causing the problem will make the ADX integration work again

example of non serializable state: 

entity_id='sensor.affalddk_road_number_farligt_affald' state='73' attributes={'date': '2024-08-29', 'date_long': 'Torsdag d. 29-08-2024', 'date_short': 'Tor d. 29/08', 'description': 'Rød boks (1 stk.)', 'duration': 'Om 73 dage', 'entity_picture': 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,', 'last_update': '2024-06-17T08:29:18.328399+02:00', 'name': 'Farligt affald', 'unit_of_measurement': 'dage', 'attribution': 'Data delivered by Danish Municipalities', 'icon': 'mdi:recycle', 'friendly_name': 'Affalddk Road Number Farligt affald'} last_changed=datetime.datetime(2024, 6, 17, 6, 29, 18, 360184, tzinfo=TzInfo(UTC)) last_updated=datetime.datetime(2024, 6, 17, 6, 29, 18, 360184, tzinfo=TzInfo(UTC)) context=Context(id='01J0JE5FWR8DYA0717QTZREFYR')

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.azure_data_explorer
Kilde: components/azure_data_explorer/__init__.py:175
integration: Azure Data Explorer (dokumentation, problemer)
Første forekomst: 8.28.21 AM (26 forekomster)
Senest logget: 9.06.46 AM

Dropped 4 old events, consider filtering messages
Dropped 1 old events, consider filtering messages
Dropped 2 old events, consider filtering messages
```


### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: Can't we change this in the library?
According to this: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/python/sdk/azure-sdk-logging this is they way. however Im now a bit more precise, using azure.kusto
Should be more specific, but already fixed with #121802. So these statements can be removed.
I don't like to patch json, is there a more real use case that can trigger this?

The usecase that I have, that actually is triggering, is having a state with a picture element. when using this, the I get an error that its too long a state, despite that is what I see in the real world. this is why I mocked the Error
What do you mean with picture element? an `image.*` entity?

This is the event that is failing, because its not serializable:

entity_id='sensor.affalddk_adress_farligt_affald' state='69' attributes={'date': '2024-08-29', 'date_long': 'Torsdag d. 29-08-2024', 'date_short': 'Tor d. 29/08', 'description': 'Rød boks (1 stk.)', 'duration': 'Om 69 dage', 'entity_picture': 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,', 'last_update': '2024-06-21T10:18:27.519373+02:00', 'name': 'Farligt affald', 'unit_of_measurement': 'dage', 'attribution': 'Data delivered by Danish Municipalities', 'icon': 'mdi:recycle', 'friendly_name': 'Affalddk adress Farligt affald'} last_changed=datetime.datetime(2024, 6, 21, 0, 18, 27, 532508, tzinfo=TzInfo(UTC)) last_updated=datetime.datetime(2024, 6, 21, 8, 18, 27, 520653, tzinfo=TzInfo(UTC)) context=Context(id='01J0WY07J0ZSEWQ57XG327CMZ0')
This is the direct output of another integration (affalddk from HACS), but as I see it, ADX needs to be able to automatically filter out stuff that for one reason or another is not serializable

Oooh, but that means you just make a sensor that properly tests this.

Like I'd rather see tests where we properly test this than to rely on json.dumps to raise an issue. It will also help with regressions in the future
I agree, but when I aplieed that exact string into the state change, I get an too long error, and the test fails without running. Im not sure for to test this without mocking the json.dumps?
Create a fake string, that is not serializable?

Tryed this: hass.states.async_set("sensor.test_sensor", b"non_serializable_event")

This will get json.dump to fail, but not within HA, it must be cast somewhere before reaching the json.dumps.

I might also be chasing chosts here, I have a hard time getting the exact error. the only problem I see is that with the above mentioned HACS integration, both this and Azure Eventhub Integration stalls, and stops sending more events. This is documented in this issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/119812

But I really dont know how to deeply debug this issue. the only error I get is after the reset of the integration I get a "x number of messegas dropped" in the log, and I can see that the memory consumption of both ADX and AEH integrations skyrockets, as it accumulates more and more messeges in memory without sending them. And ofcurse no messages is recieved in Azure. When disabling or setting a filter for this affalddk integration, the problem disapears. 

SO the only thing I actually knows is that this integration is giving me the problems, and it looks very strange in its abnormal long state

Hope you can help me

But there you're setting the state to a binary value what doesn't work. From your example I'm assuming that the binary info is the entity picture, so wouldn't setting the entity picture of an entity achieve the same?
And maybe a good temporary solution could be ignoring certain fields when serializing
